title: Freally MIDI Master StyleModel
description: A style model: numbers and rules describing a musical style. It contains no MIDI, no audio, and no transcription of any recording. See docs/legal/disclaimer.md.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema, so editors offer completion while authoring.

id.description: kebab-case, unique across the whole dataset. This is what `extends` refers to — not the filename.

aliases.description: Search synonyms, including the spellings used in producer Discord channel names.

extends.description: Ordered parents; later entries win over earlier ones, and this model wins over all of them. Genre archetypes extend `_defaults`.

relatedGenres.description: Ids of the genre models this artist works in, for cross-filtering the roster. Distinct from the two neighbouring fields it is easy to confuse it with: `genres` is free-text tags in a vocabulary of its own (`rap`, `drill`) that names no model, and `extends` is parameter inheritance — a model can only extend what it is musically built from, and the first entry here is normally that parent. Every id must name a model of type `genre`, which is checked. Curated rather than derived: an artist's tags cannot produce this, because `rap` is on almost every model and would relate everything to everything.

confidence.description: How well-sourced this model's parameters are. Low-confidence models should say why in `notes`.

sources.description: Where the parameters came from. Required in practice for any contributed model.

amount.description: MPC-style swing: 0.50 straight, 0.58 classic MPC, 0.667 full triplet. Outside 0.50–0.75 is almost always a typo.

modes.description: Named partial overrides of this model — the same author writing a different kind of record (TASK-040V). Each carries a name, a sampling weight, and any block it wants to change; the override is merged into the model before any generator runs, so every part honours a mode without knowing modes exist. Inherited through `extends` like any other block, and because arrays replace rather than append, an artist authoring its own modes replaces its genre's rather than adding to them — which is what keeps an artist's moods to the ones that artist actually does.

name.description: How the mood is named in the UI. Unique within the model.

weight.description: Relative likelihood when the seed picks. 0 means the mode exists but is only reachable by pinning it.

register.description: [low, high] as MIDI note numbers, C1 = 24.

mode.description: The style's centre of gravity, which matters as much as the bounds.

numSpec.description: A numeric parameter in any of the three authoring forms: exact, [min,max] range, or weighted choice.

strSpec.description: A categorical parameter: a bare string, or a weighted choice between strings.

drumsBlock.description: The drum block. Everything except `percs` is still open, exactly as partBlock describes — this narrows only the sub-block whose generator has landed.

percs.description: Null is how a model switches the inherited block OFF, and the schema must not be stricter than the engine: read::block in engine/src/generators/mod.rs treats an explicit null as absent, which is exactly what `"bass808": null` does in 51 shipped models. _defaults.json authors drums.percs, so this is the only way a model can decline it.

percsBlock.description: The percussion layer (TASK-140). Locked down rather than left open because the generator that reads it has landed, which is the rule partBlock states for itself. `lanes` is what this exists for: a name that is not a perc lane is dropped silently by drums::percs, which is how `woodblock` — and later `pedalHat` and `rideBell` — were authored by shipped models and never heard.

lanes.description: The voices to sprinkle. Deliberately NOT enumerated here: the list is the engine's PERC_LANES, and spelling it out again would be a second copy for a test to keep honest. dataset:validate refuses an unknown lane through the percs lint in engine/src/dataset/validate.rs, which reports this same JSON pointer with the reason. Null is accepted for the same reason percs itself is: read::strings treats a non-array as absent, so refusing it here would fail a file the engine reads correctly.

densityPerBar.description: Hits per bar, as [min, max]. Non-negative: a negative count is not a sparser layer, it is a typo.

placement.description: Which 16ths a hit may land on. `any` is the default and means a sprinkle; `downbeat` is what makes a crash authorable, since a cymbal accent is a position rather than a density.

gainOffsetDb.description: How far under the kit the layer sits, in dB — the way a producer thinks about it.

tambourine.description: A steady 8th-note tambourine. Its own flag rather than a lanes entry because it is a pulse, not a sprinkle.

tambourineMirrorsClap.description: Double every clap with a tambourine. The second of the two non-density forms, and the reason both are flags.

partBlock.description: A generator's parameter block. Deliberately open: each generator's fields are locked down as that generator lands, and the engine's lints (inverted ranges, mismatched weights, out-of-range registers and probabilities) apply everywhere in the meantime.
